sections.section_title: Initial Presentation and Sepsis Induced by Capnocytophaga canimorsus
description: Describes the patient’s clinical course from bite through septic shock.
Highlights how epidemiologic clues lead early suspicion of C.​canimorsus.
Provides key laboratory values that establish sepsis‑related coagulation derangement.
subtopics: "Dog bite timeline – symptom onset within 4 days"
"Physical exam – fever >40°C, mottled extremities, hypoglycaemia refractory to glucagon"
"Laboratory profile – pancytopenia with WBC <3 ×10⁹/L, AKI (creatinine ~170 µmol/L), transaminitis"
"Coagulation abnormalities – prolonged PT/PTT (< 70 s), low fibrinogen (<80 mg/dL), elevated d‑dimer"
"Metabolic derangement – metabolic acidosis pH 7.27 lactate 5.7 mmol/L"
"Initial diagnosis—septic shock secondary to dog bite"
"Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics covering Capnocytophaga (piperacillin/tazobactam)"
"Early suspicion of Capnocytophaga based on epidemiology despite negative culture initially"

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Challenge: Distinguishing Sepsis‑Related DIC from Thrombotic Microangiopathy
description: Explains how overlapping features forced careful exclusionary testing.
Shows stepwise use of scoring systems cut-gaps between probable etiologies.
Summarizes critical laboratory triggers that distinguished CM‑HUS.
subtopics: "Suspicion of acute leukemia or haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis ruled out by flow cytometry/bone marrow"
"Persistent thrombocytopenia despite improvements suggests ongoing microangiopathy"
"Peripheral smear evolution — schistocytes rise from <5% to 15–20% signalling MAHA"
"ADAMTS13 activity 43.5% rules out thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (<10%)"
"PLASMIC score calculated low—reduces pretest probability of TTP"
"Stool PCR negative for Shiga toxin excludes STEC‑associated HUS"
"Kidney biopsy shows ischemic glomeruli with fibrin thrombi confirming TMA histopathology"
"Integrated evidence supports CM‑HUS rather than sepsis-induced DIC alone"

sections.section_title: ’Complement-Mediated Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome’: Pathophysiology and Infection Trigger
description: "Describes genetic regulation and why infections layer onto predisposition."
Illustrates how C.​canimorsus interacts with host complement.
Synthesizes current literature linking this pathogen with CM‑HUS.
subtopics: "Alternative pathway regulated by factor H, I,B ≤ training CD46"
"50–70% heretofore patients carry genetic variants or autoantibodies”
"Infections act as second hit provoking uncontrolled endothelial injury”
"Capnocytophaga has LPS capable of triggering alternative pathway activation”
"Capsule expression confers vascular resistance yet still activate complement in susceptible hosts”
"Endothelial damage correlated with severe MAHA observed clinically”
"Literature reports support pattern from animal bites causing CM‑HUS”
"Absence of pathogenic variants confirms strict infection-triggered disease in this case”
